Product.title: Product
Product.description: Represents a single food or snack item available for ordering in the Ramadhan Takjil app.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Product entity. Corresponds to RpSKU-X in the source data.

name.description: The name of the food or snack item, e.g., 'Nasi Bakar Ayam'.

price.description: The price of one unit of the product in Indonesian Rupiah (IDR).

Customer.title: Customer
Customer.description: Stores information about a customer who places an order. This entity consolidates contact and delivery details.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Customer entity.

name.description: The full name of the customer as provided in the order form.

email.description: The email address of the customer.

phoneNumber.description: The contact phone or WhatsApp number of the customer.

deliveryAddress.description: The full address where the order should be delivered.

Order.title: Order
Order.description: Represents a single order placed by a customer, containing general order details like total amount, payment method, and delivery information.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Order entity.

customerId.description: Reference to the Customer who placed this order. (Relationship: Customer 1:N Order)

orderDateTime.description: The date and time when the order was placed.

paymentMethod.description: The chosen payment method for the order, either 'QRIS' or 'COD'.

deliveryFee.description: The fixed delivery fee applied to this order (Rp. 2,500).

totalAmount.description: The total amount of the order, including item costs and delivery fee.

status.description: The current status of the order (e.g., 'Pending', 'Confirmed', 'Delivered', 'Cancelled').

OrderItem.title: OrderItem
OrderItem.description: Represents a specific item included within a customer's order, detailing the product, quantity, and its price at the time of order.

id.description: Unique identifier for the OrderItem entity.

orderId.description: Reference to the Order this item belongs to. (Relationship: Order 1:N OrderItem)

productId.description: Reference to the Product being ordered. (Relationship: Product 1:N OrderItem)

quantity.description: The quantity of the product ordered.

unitPrice.description: The price of one unit of the product at the time the order was placed. This preserves historical price data, even if the product's price changes later.

definition.description: Stores information about available food and snack items. Documents in this collection are publicly readable by all users (authenticated or unauthenticated).

params.name: productId
params.description: The unique identifier for a specific product.

definition.description: Stores the profile information for an authenticated customer. The document ID (`userId`) corresponds to `request.auth.uid`. Includes fields like name, email, phone number, and delivery address.

params.name: userId
params.description: The unique identifier of the authenticated customer, matching `request.auth.uid`.

definition.description: Stores individual orders placed by a specific customer. The `customerId` field within each order document is denormalized to match the `userId` in the path, ensuring authorization independence.

params.name: userId
params.description: The unique identifier of the customer who placed the order.

params.name: orderId
params.description: The unique identifier for a specific order.

definition.description: Stores the details of specific items within an order. The `customerId` field is denormalized from the parent order to ensure authorization independence. Each document also includes `orderId` and `productId` references, along with quantity and unit price.

params.name: userId
params.description: The unique identifier of the customer who owns the parent order.

params.name: orderId
params.description: The unique identifier for the parent order.

params.name: orderItemId
params.description: The unique identifier for a specific item within an order.

definition.description: A collection used for Database Access Control (DBAC) to designate administrative users. The existence of a document at this path for a given UID signifies that the user is an administrator. Content of documents can be empty or contain simple role information. (Note: Using Customer schema as a placeholder for a simple existence check, actual schema could be minimal or empty).

params.name: uid
params.description: The unique identifier of a user who has an administrative role.

firestore.reasoning:
The Firestore structure is designed following the CORE DESIGN PRINCIPLES and DESIGN STRATEGY MANDATES to ensure security, scalability, and debuggability. 

**1. Authorization Independence via Denormalization:**
   *   For `Order` documents at `/users/{userId}/orders/{orderId}`, the `customerId` field will be denormalized to explicitly store the ID of the user who placed the order. This `customerId` will match the `userId` in the path, allowing security rules to directly check `request.auth.uid == resource.data.customerId` without requiring a `get()` call to a parent `User` document.
   *   For `OrderItem` documents at `/users/{userId}/orders/{orderId}/orderItems/{orderItemId}`, the `customerId` (or `orderOwnerId`) will be denormalized from the parent `Order`. This enables security rules to verify `request.auth.uid == resource.data.customerId` directly on the `OrderItem` document, eliminating `get()` calls to both `Order` and `User` documents. This is critical for robust atomic operations and simplified rule logic.

**2. Structural Segregation for QAPs (Rules are not Filters):**
   *   **Products:** Stored in a top-level collection `/products`. These items are publicly viewable by all users, so a `list` operation on this collection is inherently secure and does not require complex filtering by rules.
   *   **Customer Profiles:** Each authenticated user's profile is stored as a document at `/users/{userId}`. This path directly scopes access, meaning a `list` or `get` operation is only valid for `request.auth.uid`, thus enabling secure QAPs.
   *   **Orders:** Each customer's orders are stored in a subcollection `/users/{userId}/orders`. Access to these orders is naturally scoped by the `{userId}` wildcard, ensuring that `list` operations (e.g., fetching all orders for the current user) only return data owned by `request.auth.uid`.
   *   **Order Items:** Nested under specific orders in `/users/{userId}/orders/{orderId}/orderItems`. Their access is implicitly secured by the parent `Order`'s path, and explicitly secured by the denormalized `customerId` field, making `list` operations within an order context also secure.
   *   **Admin Roles:** A dedicated collection `/admin_roles/{uid}` uses the 'existence over content' pattern for DBAC. A `get` operation on `roles_admin/$(request.auth.uid)` securely checks if a user is an admin without needing to filter data.

This design prioritizes a clear, path-based ownership model for user-specific and nested data, combined with strategic denormalization to eliminate `get()` calls in security rules, thereby achieving high levels of security, debuggability, and performance for common query patterns and atomic writes.
